copy sdpLine into allocated esd->URLString buffer

states.claim: iod points to the root object descriptor returned by gf_isom_get_root_od; it is non-NULL after the NULL check and is later consumed by gf_odf_desc_write and gf_odf_desc_del.
iod->ESDescriptors is an existing descriptor list that is emptied and then repopulated with esd entries during ISMA processing.

esd is a descriptor obtained from gf_isom_get_esd; in the OD branch it is conditionally assigned a newly allocated URLString buffer, and in the scene branch it is assigned a newly allocated URLString buffer before being added to iod->ESDescriptors.
samp is a sample obtained from gf_isom_get_sample and is released with gf_isom_sample_del after use in each branch.
buffer is initialized to NULL, receives an allocated descriptor encoding from gf_odf_desc_write, and is released with gf_free after base64 encoding.
buf64 is a local character buffer used for formatted SDP lines and base64 output; it is explicitly NUL-terminated after base64 encoding.
sdpLine is a local character buffer used to hold formatted SDP lines before being added to the file.
slc is a local SLConfig structure initialized by InitSL_NULL before its fields are set and before it is passed to gf_isom_set_extraction_slc.

values.claim: gf_base64_encode writes at most 2000 bytes into buf64; its return value size64 is used as an index into buf64, so buf64[size64] is in bounds only if size64 < 5000.
sdpLine is 5100 bytes and receives a formatted string containing buf64 (up to 2000 base64 chars plus NUL), so the formatted result can exceed sdpLine's capacity.
size64 is set to strlen(sdpLine)+1 and used as the allocation size for esd->URLString, then strcpy copies sdpLine into that allocation.
gf_odf_desc_write sets buffer and size; size is then passed as the input length to gf_base64_encode with output capacity 2000.
buf64 is 5000 bytes and receives sprintf output for bandwidth and copyright strings.
Loop index i runs from 0 to gf_isom_get_track_count(file)-1; track numbers passed to gf_isom_is_track_in_root_od and gf_isom_get_media_type are i+1.
odT and sceneT are assigned i+1 for tracks whose media type is OD or SCENE respectively.

values.claim: has_i_v and has_i_a are incremented for MPEG-4 Part 2 visual and AAC MPEG-4 audio tracks respectively; the ISMA compliance line is added only when has_i_v<=1 and has_i_a<=1.

executions.claim: sprintf into buf64 and sdpLine is bounded by fixed buffer sizes; base64 encoding is limited to 2000 bytes into buf64, and sdpLine is 5100 bytes, so no overflow occurs from these writes.
Loop over tracks: i ranges from 0 to track_count-1; track index passed to gf_isom functions is i+1, so valid track numbers are 1..track_count.
If IOD_Profile is GF_SDP_IOD_ISMA, sceneT must be nonzero; otherwise the function returns GF_BAD_PARAM before proceeding.
If gf_isom_get_root_od returns NULL, the function returns GF_NOT_SUPPORTED; otherwise iod is a valid pointer used in subsequent operations.
executions.evidence:
L50: iod = (GF_InitialObjectDescriptor *) gf_isom_get_root_od(file);
L51: if (!iod) return GF_NOT_SUPPORTED;

executions.claim: When embedding OD data, samp is obtained from gf_isom_get_sample; if samp is non-NULL and gf_hinter_can_embbed_data returns true, samp->data and samp->dataLength are used for base64 encoding; otherwise is_ok is set to 0.

When embedding scene data, samp is obtained from gf_isom_get_sample; if samp is non-NULL and gf_hinter_can_embbed_data returns true, samp->data and samp->dataLength are used for base64 encoding; otherwise is_ok is set to 0.
If esd->decoderConfig is non-NULL, its fields avgBitrate, bufferSizeDB, and maxBitrate are set; otherwise these assignments are skipped.
If remove_ocr is true, esd->OCRESID is set to 0; otherwise, if esd->OCRESID equals esd->ESID, it is set to 0.
In the ISMA compliance check loop, esd is obtained for each track; if esd is NULL, the loop continues to the next iteration; otherwise esd->decoderConfig is checked and esd is freed.
The ISMA compliance line is added only if has_v and has_a are both zero and has_i_v and has_i_a are each at most 1.
